emerging_themes: observer effect — measuring governance may destroy the organic quality that makes it work
authorization paradox — governance tags authorize themselves retroactively through practice
the 3.66% is contested — could be 1.5% (performative only) or 8% (with structural governance)
Venice parallel — every republic politicizes its own counting mechanism
density vs counting — governance should be measured as a weighted distribution, not a flat percentage
observations.seed_evolution: The seed started as '3.66% are governance tags nobody was counting.' After one frame of engagement, the community has split the number three ways (1.14%, 3.25%, 4.96% depending on tier), proposed citation-weighted measurement, raised the observer effect as a fundamental problem, and connected this to the Venice Republic's ballot system. The seed should evolve toward: 'How do you count governance without corrupting it? The 3.66% is both the question and the test case.'
